title: People’s Mañanera September 18
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity 's Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available [here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Guanajuato: Homicides Down 75%  
** In the state of Guanajuato, homicides decreased from 12.7 to 3.2 per day,
and high-impact crimes dropped by 43%. President Claudia Sheinbaum emphasized
that this is the result of "addressing the root causes and coordination. We
have to keep working. It's a daily effort."

**Blow to Fuel Theft: 59 Million Liters Seized  
** The seizure was the result of a coordinated investigation that revealed the
origin and destination of the fuel. Sheinbaum emphasized that "it's important
to us that those involved in the illegal purchase and sale of fuel are
apprehended."

**USMCA Remains in Effect: Mexico and the U.S. Make Progress on Trade
Agreement  
** Following her telephone call with U.S. President Donald Trump, Sheinbaum
reported that good progress is being made on the agreement and that Mexico
seeks to reduce tariffs on steel, aluminum, and automobiles. The USMCA has not
formally been scrapped, and efforts are being made to maintain the treaty.

**Health: 11% Budget Increase and New Infrastructure  
** The President confirmed that there is a Mexican Social Security Institute
(IMSS) project for Celaya and that she will review hospital needs in Irapuato.
She indicated that there are sufficient resources and that, after decades of
neglect, former president Andrés Manuel López Obrador "left behind a better
healthcare system than the one he inherited."

**Mexico City -Irapuato-Leon-Guadalajara Train: Project Confirmed  
**Sheinbaum confirmed that the passenger train will connect Mexico City,
Irapuato, Leon, and Guadalajara. The project has already been designed, and
the bidding process will move forward this year. In addition, San Miguel de
Allende will have a station on the route to San Luis Potosi.
